the 4-aryl derivatives of 2-methylthiomethyl-2-imidazole are synthesized by the reaction of cis- and tranc-3-aroyl aziridine complexes with boron trifluore and methyl thiocyanates, which are opened at the C-2 atom of the aziridine cycle with inversion of configuration.
the 4-aryl-substituted 5-aroylthio-2-aziridinylimidazolines are formed by the reaction of 3-aroylaziri­dines and boron tri­fluoride with methylthio­cyanate.

the aziridines react with methyl thiocarbonates in the presence of boron trifluorethylate with opening of the aziridine rings to give 2-imidazolidinethiones.
the reaction of the cis-isomer with methyl thiocyanoate leads to the formation of the 4-aryl derivative, while the reaction of the trans-isomer leads to the formation 5-aryl derivative.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3-aryl-5-aryloxymethylaziridine-2-carboxylates 1-3 are readily available by reaction of the appropriate arylacetonitrile with the corresponding 3-arylaziridine-1-carboxylates, and that the reaction proceeds with retention of configuration.
we were able to show that the aziridines are opened regioselectively at C2, and stereoselectively with inversion of stereochemistry.
the aziridines are not only opened regio- and stereospecific but that this opening is accompanied by the migration of an aryl substituent from the C(2)- to the C(5) position of the imidazole ring.
